evidence.excerpt: The conventional PAF model accumulates failure costs by financial value without weighting for downstream consequence severity. A tombstoning defect detected at final test costs roughly the same in rework labour as a bridging defect, yet the bridging defect may carry higher field-failure risk if it escapes to the customer. This paper proposes an augmented PAF formulation in which each failure cost event is multiplied by a severity weight derived from an FMEA-style consequence scale anchored to field return data. The model is parameterised using 26 months of defect, rework, and field return records from a surface-mount technology line producing industrial sensor modules. Incorporating severity weights shifts the Pareto ranking of defect categories: solder voids on BGAs rise from fourth to first priority, while tombstoning falls from first to third. Re-prioritising corrective investment according to the severity-weighted ranking reduces estimated expected field failure cost by 17% relative to the unweighted ranking, at the same total corrective expenditure. The paper discusses the sensitivity of the results to severity score uncertainty and provides a worked numerical example.
